A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ToolDelete research and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Content can be matched reliably across formatting changes, relocations, and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original tool-unlearning experiments, including baseline comparisons, component ablations, membership-inference evaluation, sequential deletion, and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and the appendices, including the ToolAlpaca comparisons and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The tool-free response targets, SFT and DPO variants, retained-tool training, task-arithmetic adjustment, and LiRA-Tool shadow-sample procedure remain unchanged. Added explanations do not establish a procedural modification.

E1.justification: The reported datasets and tasks remain ToolAlpaca, ToolBench, API-Bench, MMLU, BBH-Hard, and IFEval. Although v2's abstract adds class-specific unlearning, no corresponding experiment or identifiable class-specific results appear in the main text or appendices.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Retrain, GradAscent, RandLabel, SalUn, ICUL, SGA, TAU, CUT, NPO, and SOUL-GradDiff. Appendix B adds an explanation of CUT, but its participation and reported results are unchanged.

E3.justification: Both versions specify the same 7B models, random deletion of 2–20% of tools, general-capability evaluations, and LiRA-Tool testing at FPR = 0.01 with shadow-model forget-set sizes of 1, 5, 10, and 20. No changed experimental protocol is documented.

E4.justification: Component ablations, sequential deletion, LoRA, training-data availability, tool-free response sources, and efficiency analyses are retained. Figure 3 moves from the appendix into the main text without changing the analysis. Newly discussed adversarial evaluation remains future work.

E5.justification: Figure 2 retains the same error bars, and neither version explains their estimation or provides repeated-run or seed counts. No new uncertainty-reporting practice or statistical procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: The introduction replaces v1's unfinished '+' comparison with reported accuracy advantages of 12.5 on forget tools and 9.1 on retained tools, without identifying their comparison or aggregation basis. Matched numerical tables and plotted results are unchanged; these are new summary assertions, not demonstrated performance improvements between versions.

T1.justification: Definitions 3.1–3.3 and Equations 1–8 retain their mathematical content. v2 explains the existing P_U and P_Tr symbols after Equation 8, but introduces no new formal property, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract expands the claimed demonstrated capability from randomly selected tools to both random and class-specific tools. The introduction also quantifies its previously incomplete superiority claim. The central contributions—tool unlearning, ToolDelete, and LiRA-Tool—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly identifies adversarial evaluation as an outstanding limitation and adds loss-landscape analysis to future work. It also expands the mechanism discussion to contrast calibrated forgetting with both over- and under-unlearning. Existing limitations concerning shadow samples, closed-source models, and model scale remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the learning rate of 10^-5, eight NVIDIA A100 GPUs, and the same public checkpoint identifiers. Appendix E preserves the substantive GPT-4 shadow-sample prompt. No new implementation settings or resource-access information are supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds works by Lynch, Łucki, Hu, Fan on relearning resistance, and Cheng and Amiri on mode connectivity to support robustness discussion and future directions. The overall research positioning remains stable; publication updates to existing references are not new cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract and impact statement are rewritten, with localized edits to the results discussion and related work. LiRA notation and the CUT baseline receive short explanations. The main section sequence and Appendix A–E organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference paper with running headers and extensively reflowed figures, tables, and equations. Figure 3 moves into the main text. Appendix Tables 5–7 become Tables 7, 5, and 6 respectively, while their content is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful explanatory and citation updates, but weakens alignment between claims and evidence: its abstract newly claims class-specific unlearning without a corresponding reported experiment, and its new 12.5/9.1 accuracy advantages lack an identified supporting comparison. With the experimental evidence unchanged, these reporting problems outweigh the limited gains in clarity and presentation.
